full_text_en:
Nikon Corporation v. Zhejiang Nikon Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd. et al. — Dispute over Infringement of Registered Trademark Rights and Unfair Competition

【Ruling Summary】

I. Where the alleged infringer uses a well-known trademark on goods that are not identical or similar, and such use is sufficient to cause the relevant public to believe that the accused trademark has a considerable degree of association with the well-known trademark, thereby weakening the distinctiveness of the well-known trademark, cross-class protection shall be granted to the well-known trademark. Where finding some trademarks to be well-known is sufficient to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the registered trademark owner, it is unnecessary to determine whether the remaining trademarks are well-known. Whether a trademark is well-known shall be determined as of the time when the alleged act of trademark infringement or unfair competition occurred.

II. When hearing a case involving a conflict between a registered trademark right and a right to a company name, if the company's trade name is sufficient to cause the relevant public to be confused or mistaken as to the provider of the goods or services, the court shall order the infringer to cease using that trade name.

Plaintiff: Nikon Corporation, domiciled at Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Japan.
Legal Representative: Ichiro Teradono, Representative Director and Vice President of the company.

Defendant: Xi'an Taihua Electric Bicycle Wholesale Market Co., Ltd., domiciled at Taihua Road, Xincheng District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Zaixin, Executive Director and General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Zhu Guoping, male, 48 years old, domiciled at Yeming Village, Dongxiao Subdistrict, Jindong District, Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province.

Defendant: Zhejiang Nikon Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd., domiciled at Chisong Road, Jindong New District Industrial Park, Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Li Ming, Executive Director and General Manager of the company.

The plaintiff, Nikon Corporation, filed a lawsuit with the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province against the defendants, Xi'an Taihua Electric Bicycle Wholesale Market Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taihua Market), Zhu Guoping, and Zhejiang Nikon Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhejiang Nikon), concerning a dispute over infringement of registered trademark rights and unfair competition.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** On August 15, 1979, the plaintiff obtained the registered trademark "Nikon"; on February 15, 1986, the plaintiff obtained the registered trademark "尼康"; and on September 7, 2004, the plaintiff obtained the registered trademark "Nikon" for digital cameras. In 1985, the plaintiff established a representative office in Beijing, and starting in 1992, the plaintiff established several companies named "尼康" in Shanghai and other locations. The plaintiff has invested substantial funds in brand promotion and product advertising in mainland China, and "尼康" cameras enjoy a very high market share in China. In April 2009, the trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon" were recognized as well-known trademarks by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as SAIC). The Nikon electric vehicles sold by the defendants Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping were produced by the defendant Zhejiang Nikon, and these products used the trademarks "尼康" and "NICOM". Zhejiang Nikon prominently used the words "尼康" and "NICOM" on its store signs and promotional posters. The plaintiff contends that the defendants, without authorization, commercially used signs identical or similar to the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks, and produced and sold products bearing signs identical or similar to those trademarks. Such conduct is sufficient to cause the relevant public to be confused about the source of the defendants' goods and services, or to mistakenly believe that the defendants have some connection with the plaintiff, thereby infringing the plaintiff's trademark rights to "尼康" and "Nikon". Furthermore, Zhejiang Nikon's use of "尼康" as its corporate trade name is sufficient to cause the relevant public to believe that the defendants and their goods and services have a specific connection with the plaintiff, constituting unfair competition. The plaintiff requests the court to order: Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping to cease selling electric vehicle products that infringe the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon"; Zhejiang Nikon to cease the acts infringing the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon"; Zhejiang Nikon to cease the unfair competition act of using the characters "尼康" in its corporate name; and Zhejiang Nikon to compensate the plaintiff for losses in the amount of RMB 2,000,000.

The plaintiff, Nikon Corporation, provided the following seven sets of evidence:

**First Set:** Trademark registration certificates and renewal certificates for "尼康" (No. 243268), "Nikon" (No. 97095), and "Nikon" (No. 3427916). Used to prove that it obtained the exclusive right to use the trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon".

**Second Set:**  
1. Trademark registration certificates for "尼康" and "Nikon" in different classes, and trademark licensing contracts. Used to prove that the plaintiff, Nikon Corporation, registered the trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon" in over 40 classes of goods in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, and the duration of use of the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks in China.  
2. Industrial and commercial registration files and notarized certificates of Nikon Corporation's Chinese subsidiaries. Used to prove the sales regions, sales amounts, and profits of goods bearing the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks in China; and the ranking of Nikon Corporation in the "Most Concerned Digital Camera Brands by Chinese Users" over the years.  
3. Advertising contracts, newspapers and magazines carrying print advertisements, materials from exhibitions and competitions, outdoor advertising photos, and advertising videos. Used to prove the advertising and promotion of Nikon Corporation's "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks and related products, and the extremely high reputation of the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks in China.  
4. Rulings on trademark disputes and trademark oppositions, and administrative documents on the investigation and seizure of counterfeit products in various locations in China. Used to prove the extremely high reputation of Nikon Corporation's "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks in China and the record of protection as well-known trademarks.  
5. Certificates of honor, medals, and trophies. Used to prove that Nikon Corporation and the goods bearing the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks have won various awards in China and enjoy a very high reputation in the same industry and among consumers.  
This set of evidence is used to prove that the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks (Class 9) are well-known in China.

**Third Set:**  
1. Documents proving Nikon Corporation's registration of the "Nikon" trademark in Japan and other countries worldwide, and annual reports.  
2. Sales regions, sales amounts, and profits of goods bearing the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks worldwide.  
3. Media reports on Nikon Corporation's "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks and related products.  
This set of evidence is used to prove that the "尼康" and "Nikon" trademarks (Class 9) are well-known worldwide.

**Fourth Set:**  
1. The "Current Matters Full Certificate" of the plaintiff, Nikon Corporation.  
2. Copies of business licenses and certificates of approval for foreign-invested enterprises of Nikon Corporation's Chinese subsidiaries.  
This set of evidence is used to prove that Nikon Corporation enjoys the right to its corporate name.

**Fifth Set:**  
1. Industrial and commercial registration materials of the defendant Zhejiang Nikon. Used to prove the date of establishment of Zhejiang Nikon.  
2. Notarized certificates, "Nikon News", advertisements for Nikon electric vehicles, and other materials. Used to prove that Zhejiang Nikon used the words "尼康" and "NICOM" on its company website, in external promotions, in store decorations, and on products, thereby infringing the trademark rights to "尼康" and "Nikon".  
3. Industrial and commercial registration materials of the defendant Taihua Market. Used to prove the date of establishment of Taihua Market.  
4. After-sales service vouchers. Used to prove that Taihua Market and the Jinnikon Electric Bicycle Shop jointly sold electric bicycles using the words "尼康" and "NICOM", thereby infringing the plaintiff Nikon Corporation's trademark rights to "尼康" and "Nikon".  
5. Application for registration of individual industrial and commercial household and lease contract. Used to prove that the owner of the Xi'an Xincheng District Jinnikon Electric Bicycle Shop is the defendant Zhu Guoping, who engages in the wholesale and retail sale of electric bicycles; and that Zhu Guoping sold electric bicycles bearing the trademark "尼康" and "NICOM", thereby infringing Nikon Corporation's trademark rights to "尼康" and "Nikon".  
6. Notarized certificates. Used to prove that Zhejiang Nikon, without authorization, used the words "尼康", "NICOM", and "Zhejiang Nikon Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd." on its company website, constituting unfair competition against Nikon Corporation.  
7. Industrial and commercial archive materials of Zhejiang Nikon. Used to prove that in 2006, Zhejiang Nikon changed its name from "Jinhua Five-Star Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd." to its current name. Zhejiang Nikon's use of "尼康" as its corporate trade name constitutes unfair competition against Nikon Corporation.  
8. Notarized web pages. Used to prove that Nikon electric vehicles produced by Zhejiang Nikon have been complained about by consumers due to quality issues; and that consumers mistakenly believe that Nikon electric vehicles are products of Nikon Corporation or have a specific connection with it.  
9. Trademark dispute ruling. Used to prove that the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board (TRAB) of SAIC lawfully revoked the disputed trademark "尼康 and device" (No. 1977805); and that Zhejiang Nikon had subjective bad faith in infringing Nikon Corporation's trademark rights to "尼康" and engaging in unfair competition.

**Sixth Set:**  
1. Annual inspection reports of the defendant Zhejiang Nikon.  
2. Agreement for hiring a lawyer and lawyer fee invoices.  
3. After-sales service vouchers for electric bicycles and notarization fee invoices.  
4. Travel expense invoices.  
5. Document retrieval fee invoices.  
6. Translation fee invoices.  
Used to prove Zhejiang Nikon's profits from infringement and the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation in stopping the infringing acts.

**Seventh Set:**  
1. Evidence showing that the plaintiff Nikon Corporation established a permanent representative office in Beijing. Used to prove that Nikon Corporation established a representative office in China on December 18, 1985.  
2. Administrative judgment No. (2010) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 1136 of the Beijing High People's Court. Used to prove that Nikon Corporation's trademarks "Nikon" (No. 97095) and "尼康" (No. 243268) are well-known trademarks on cameras and other goods; and that the defendant Zhejiang Nikon's trademark "尼康 and device" (No. 1977805) was lawfully revoked.

**Defendant Taihua Market's Defense:** When Nikon electric vehicles entered the market operated by the defendant, they had already obtained the relevant licenses and permits and were lawful goods; the business scope of Taihua Market is market construction and development, and leasing of houses and facilities, not the sale of electric bicycles. The after-sales vouchers provided by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation are an act of misleading Taihua Market, and the special administrative seal cannot be used as evidence of sales; Taihua Market has not committed any infringing act, so there is no need to cease infringement; the court is requested to reject the plaintiff's claims.

The defendant Taihua Market submitted the following evidence:

1. Site lease contract. Used to prove that it had a lease relationship, not a cooperative relationship, with the defendant Zhu Guoping.
2. "Certificate" and "Explanation". Used to prove that it had terminated the lease relationship with the defendant Zhu Guoping.
3. Business license of the individual industrial and commercial household, business license of the defendant Zhejiang Nikon, production permit, and honorary certificates. Used to prove that the defendant Taihua Market operated lawfully and fulfilled its duty of care in examination.

The defendant Zhu Guoping did not submit a defense or any evidence.

**Defendant Zhejiang Nikon's Defense:** The trademarks used by Zhejiang Nikon were lawfully obtained; the plaintiff Nikon Corporation's "尼康" and "Nikon" are not well-known trademarks; Zhejiang Nikon has a lawful trade name and does not constitute unfair competition; in its use of the trademarks, Zhejiang Nikon neither caused misleading or confusion nor engaged in free-riding; the court is requested to reject the plaintiff's claims.

The defendant Zhejiang Nikon provided relevant honorary certificates. Used to prove that Zhejiang Nikon has good product quality and commercial reputation, and that it could not possibly harm the commercial reputation of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation.

**Facts Found by the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court at First Instance:**

**1. Facts regarding the plaintiff Nikon Corporation's registered trademarks in China**

On August 15, 1979, Nippon Kogaku Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha (Japan Optical Industries Co., Ltd.) obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Nikon" upon approval by the Trademark Office of SAIC, with the designated goods being "cameras, motion picture cameras, etc." in Class 9 of the Classification of Similar Goods and Services. The trademark registration certificate is No. 97095. On August 4, 1988, upon approval by the Trademark Office, the registrant of the above trademark was changed to Nikon Corporation. Subsequently, upon approval by the Trademark Office, Nikon Corporation renewed the registration of trademark No. 97095, extending the validity period to August 14, 2019.

On February 15, 1986, Nippon Kogaku Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "尼康" upon approval by the Trademark Office, with the designated goods being "cameras, etc." in Class 9 of the Classification of Similar Goods and Services. The trademark registration certificate is No. 243268. On August 4, 1988, upon approval by the Trademark Office, the registrant of the above trademark was changed to Nikon Corporation. Subsequently, upon approval by the Trademark Office, Nikon Corporation renewed the registration of trademark No. 243268, extending the validity period to February 14, 2016.

On September 7, 2004, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Nikon" upon approval by the Trademark Office, with the designated goods being "cameras (photography), digital cameras, etc." in Class 9 of the Classification of Similar Goods and Services. The trademark registration certificate is No. 3427916, with the validity period up to September 6, 2014.

**2. Facts regarding the plaintiff Nikon Corporation's establishment of companies in China**

On December 18, 1985, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation (formerly Nippon Kogaku Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha), upon approval by SAIC, registered and established the Nikon Corporation Beijing Representative Office, with the business scope being liaison and technical exchange for optical instruments and other businesses. From March 1996 onward, Nikon Corporation successively registered and established in China: Guangdong Nikon Camera Co., Ltd.; Nanjing Nikon Jiangnan Optical Instrument Co., Ltd.; Hangzhou Nikon Camera Co., Ltd.; Nikon Optical Instruments (China) Co., Ltd.; Dongguan Nikon Electronic Measuring Instruments Co., Ltd.; Shanghai Nikon Precision Machinery Co., Ltd.; Nikon Instruments (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.; Nikon Imaging Instruments Sales (China) Co., Ltd.; and Nikon International Trading (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. During the period from September 11, 1995, to December 15, 2008, Nikon Corporation entered into trademark licensing agreements with Chinese companies such as Nanjing Jiangnan Optoelectronics (Group) Co., Ltd., licensing them to use the registered trademarks "尼康" and "Nikon" and the corporate trade name "尼康".

**3. Facts regarding the plaintiff Nikon Corporation's promotion of its products in China**

From June 1995 to October 2008, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation engaged in outdoor advertising using neon signs in Shanghai, Beijing, Xi'an, and other locations, and placed television commercials on China Central Television and over 20 provincial and municipal television stations in Beijing and other regions; it also placed online advertisements on well-known websites such as Sina, Sohu, and Baidu. Between 1980 and 2009, Nikon Corporation published print advertisements in Chinese periodicals and newspapers such as *Photography & Video*, *Popular Photography*, *Camera*, *China Trademark*, *Beijing Youth Daily*, *Xinmin Evening News*, and *Yangcheng Evening News*, promoting its products. Nikon Corporation promoted "尼康" and "Nikon" products by establishing product showrooms in China, participating in various large-scale exhibitions, and organizing various promotional activities; it sponsored various large international sports events in China to promote the "尼康" and "Nikon" brands. Nikon Corporation promoted Nikon products and brand image in the form of concerts and appointed image ambassadors. The sales scope of Nikon Corporation's products covers all regions of China. From 2003 to 2008, the "尼康" cameras produced by Nikon Corporation consistently ranked in the top five among the most concerned digital camera brands by Chinese users over the years, ranked in the top three in the brand attention ranking for single-lens reflex (SLR) digital cameras in the Chinese market, and ranked first for long-zoom digital cameras; since 2004, Nikon Corporation has won various awards in China, such as the "Reader's Most Trusted Digital Camera Brand Award", and enjoys a very high reputation in the same industry and among consumer groups.

**4. Facts regarding the registration of the defendants Zhejiang Nikon, Taihua Market, and Zhu Guoping**

On March 28, 2000, Jinhua Five-Star Elevator Co., Ltd. was registered and established. On May 28, 2001, the enterprise name was changed to Jinhua Five-Star Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd. On July 30, 2004, the enterprise name was changed to Zhejiang Jinhua Five-Star Electric Vehicle Co., Ltd. On June 27, 2006, the enterprise name was changed again to Zhejiang Nikon, with the business scope being the manufacture and sale of electric bicycles and battery-powered mopeds. In May 2008, "Nikon Electric Bicycle" was recognized as a well-known commodity of Jinhua City by the Jinhua Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce; in October 2008, the defendant Zhejiang Nikon's "Nikon Xiaoxuanfeng Electric Bicycle" won the Innovative Product Award at the 29th China Zhejiang International Bicycle and Electric Bicycle Exhibition; in November 2008, Zhejiang Nikon was recognized as having a well-known trademark of Jinhua City by the Jinhua Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce.

The defendant Taihua Market was established on September 18, 2006, with the business scope being market construction and development, leasing of market houses and facilities, and market property management. The owner of the Xi'an Xincheng District Jinnikon Electric Bicycle Shop is the defendant Zhu Guoping, who is mainly engaged in the wholesale and retail sale of electric bicycles. On April 16, 2007, Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping entered into a site lease contract, whereby Zhu Guoping leased Site A-26 of Taihua Market for operating the Zhejiang Nikon brand bicycles. On May 24, 2009, Zhu Guoping terminated the lease relationship with Taihua Market.

**5. Other facts of this case**

The defendant Zhejiang Nikon used the words "尼康" and "NICOM" on the pages of its website, in store decoration designs, etc.; among these, the "Product Introduction" section on the website introduced products produced by Zhejiang Nikon named with "Nikon", including "Nikon Tianwang II", "Nikon Golden Bull", "Nikon Xiaoying Hao", "Nikon Century Princess", etc. The product images showed that the bodies of the electric bicycles and electric tricycles produced by Zhejiang Nikon bore the words "尼康" and "NICOM". Zhejiang Nikon used the words "尼康车业" (Nikon Vehicle Industry), "尼康电动自行车" (Nikon Electric Bicycle), and "尼康" (Nikon) at the entrance of its company, on the exterior of its building, on the bodies of its company vehicles, in advertising materials, and in the "Nikon News".

On April 15, 2009, Shanghai Huacheng Law Firm went to the Nikon electric vehicle sales counter located in the defendant Taihua Market on Taihua Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, and requested product brochures from the defendant Zhejiang Nikon, and purchased two Nikon TDP40Z electric vehicles at unit prices of RMB 2,100 and RMB 2,550 respectively, and obtained the *Electric Bicycle After-Sales Service Voucher* bearing the seals of "Xi'an Xincheng District Jinnikon Electric Bicycle Shop" and "Xi'an Taihua Electric Bicycle Wholesale Market Co., Ltd. Administrative Special Seal". The storefront advertising board of Taihua Market read: "China Nikon Electric Vehicle Seeks Dealers from Various Regions Nationwide", signed as "Xi'an Office", with the words "Nikon" and "NICOM" prominently highlighted in distinctive fonts.

During the trial, because the defendant Zhejiang Nikang did not recognize that the registered trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon", No. 3427916 "Nikon", and No. 243268 "Nikon" (Chinese: 尼康) were well-known trademarks, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation applied to the court to recognize the trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon", No. 3427916 "Nikon", and No. 243268 "Nikon" as well-known trademarks.

VI. Facts Concerning the Registered Trademark of the Defendant Zhejiang Nikang — "Nikang and Design"

On August 27, 2001, Jinhua Wuxing Electric Vehicles Co., Ltd. filed an application with the Trademark Office for registration of the trademark "Nikang and Design". On December 7, 2002, it obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Nikang and Design" for use on the goods "electric vehicles, electric motorcycles, etc." in Class 12 of the Classification of Similar Goods and Services. The trademark registration certificate No. 1977805 had a validity period ending December 6, 2012. On November 29, 2006, with the approval of the Trademark Office, Jinhua Wuxing Electric Vehicles Co., Ltd. changed the registrant of the above trademark to Zhejiang Nikang.

On December 5, 2007, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation filed a revocation application against Trademark No. 1977805. On May 18, 2009, the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board ruled to revoke Trademark No. 1977805 "Nikang and Design" according to law. Zhejiang Nikang, dissatisfied with the trademark dispute ruling, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court. On December 29, 2009, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered a judgment upholding the ruling of the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board. Zhejiang Nikang appealed, and on December 14, 2010, the Beijing High People's Court rendered a judgment dismissing the appeal and upholding the first-instance judgment.

The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether the trademarks in dispute in this case should be recognized as well-known trademarks; (2) Whether the alleged infringing acts of the defendants infringed the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks enjoyed by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation; (3) Whether Zhejiang Nikang's use of the characters "Nikang" in its enterprise name constituted unfair competition; (4) Assumption of civil liability.

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

**I. Regarding whether the trademarks in dispute in this case should be recognized as well-known trademarks**

The registered trademarks "Nikon" and "Nikang" (Chinese: 尼康) have a long history of use on cameras and have achieved high visibility among consumers. The extent to which the relevant public is aware of "Nikon" and "Nikang" brand cameras is a well-known fact, meaning that the registered trademarks "Nikon" and "Nikang" have already attained a well-known status. Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks stipulates that the similar goods referred to in Article 52(1) of the Trademark Law refer to goods that are identical in function, use, production department, sales channel, consumer object, etc., or that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion. Electric vehicles and cameras have significant differences in function, use, production department, sales channel, consumer object, etc., and thus are not similar goods.

Article 13 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that where a trademark applied for registration on dissimilar goods is a reproduction, imitation, or translation of another person's well-known trademark already registered in China, misleading the public and potentially harming the interests of the registrant of the well-known trademark, the trademark shall not be registered and its use shall be prohibited. Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes Involving the Protection of Well-Known Trademarks stipulates that where it is sufficient to cause the relevant public to believe that the accused trademark has a considerable degree of connection with the well-known trademark, thereby diluting the distinctiveness of the well-known trademark, damaging the market reputation of the well-known trademark, or unfairly exploiting the market reputation of the well-known trademark, this constitutes "misleading the public, potentially harming the interests of the registrant of the well-known trademark" as provided in Article 13(2) of the Trademark Law. In this case, the defendant Zhejiang Nikang's enterprise name used the trade name "Wuxing" for six consecutive years from March 2000 until June 2006, when it began using the trade name "Nikang" and named its products "NICOM" and "Nikang". Subjectively, it had an obvious intent to free-ride; objectively, it borrowed the reputation of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation, which could potentially cause consumers to associate the market entity and the source of its goods with Nikon Corporation, thereby potentially harming the interests of Nikon Corporation.

Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes Involving the Protection of Well-Known Trademarks stipulates that if a trademark was recognized as well-known by a people's court or the administrative department for industry and commerce under the State Council before the alleged trademark infringement or unfair competition act occurred, and the defendant does not object to the fact of the well-known status of the trademark, the people's court shall recognize it. If the defendant raises an objection, the plaintiff shall still bear the burden of proof regarding the fact of the well-known status of the trademark. In this case, the registered trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon" and No. 243268 "Nikang" owned by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation were previously recognized as well-known trademarks by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce. Because the defendant Zhejiang Nikang did not recognize this fact, Nikon Corporation applied in court for a ruling to recognize the trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon", No. 243268 "Nikang", and No. 3427916 "Nikon" as well-known trademarks. According to Article 2(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes Involving the Protection of Well-Known Trademarks, in the following civil disputes, where a party uses the well-known status of a trademark as a factual basis, the people's court may, if it deems it necessary under the specific circumstances of the case, determine whether the involved trademark is well-known: infringement actions based on violation of Article 13 of the Trademark Law; infringement or unfair competition actions based on the enterprise name being identical or similar to the well-known trademark. In this case, because Zhejiang Nikang used "Nikang" as an enterprise name and on the electric bicycles it produced, Nikon Corporation requested the recognition of "Nikon" and "Nikang" as well-known trademarks. This complies with the above legal provisions, so it is necessary to examine and determine whether the trademarks in dispute are well-known.

According to Article 4 of the above interpretation, which provides that "when a people's court determines whether a trademark is well-known, it shall take the facts proving its well-known status as the basis and comprehensively consider the factors provided in Article 14 of the Trademark Law, except where it is sufficient to determine the well-known status of the trademark without considering all the factors provided in that article based on the specific circumstances of the case," because the registered trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon" and No. 243268 "Nikang" in dispute in this case have already achieved high visibility among consumers, and the relevant public has broad awareness of "Nikon" and "Nikang" brand cameras, the registered trademarks "Nikon" and "Nikang" have already attained a well-known status, meeting the standards for recognition of well-known trademarks under the above legal provisions. Therefore, it should be determined according to law that the registered trademarks No. 97095 "Nikon" and No. 243268 "Nikang" constitute well-known trademarks on camera products. As for the registered trademark No. 3427916 "Nikon", since the recognition of the above two trademarks as well-known is sufficient to protect the legitimate rights and interests of Nikon Corporation, there is no need to further determine whether this trademark is well-known. The defendant Zhejiang Nikang argued that the plaintiff Nikon Corporation was not a well-known trademark in 2001. Since the determination of whether a trademark is well-known should be based on whether the trademark was well-known at the time of the alleged infringement or unfair competition act, Zhejiang Nikang's defense lacks factual basis.

**II. Regarding whether the defendants infringed the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Nikang" and "Nikon" owned by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation**

According to law, whether the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is infringed shall be comprehensively judged based on the general attention of ordinary consumers and the above legal provisions, conducting an overall comparison and a comparison of the main parts of the trademarks in dispute. In cases of trademark infringement disputes, to determine whether the accused infringing trademark is similar to the registered trademark for which rights are claimed, consideration shall be given to the specific circumstances such as the distinctiveness and market visibility of the involved trademarks or their constituent elements, and on the basis of considering and comparing the shape, pronunciation, and meaning of the characters, the composition and color of the graphics, or the combination structure of the constituent elements, a comprehensive analysis and judgment shall be made on whether the overall or main parts have the possibility of market confusion. If the overall or main parts have the possibility of market confusion, similarity may be found; otherwise, similarity shall not be found. In determining similarity in cases of infringement of exclusive rights to use a registered trademark, it is not limited to overall similarity but also includes similarity of the main parts. When determining trademark similarity, consideration should be given to the distinctiveness and visibility of the trademark sought to be protected. In this case, the registered trademarks "Nikon" and "Nikang" approved and registered by the Trademark Office and owned by the plaintiff Nikon Corporation consist of English letters and Chinese characters respectively. Through Nikon Corporation's use, advertising, and the market share of its products, these registered trademarks, due to their long registration period, good market reputation, and high frequency of use, have high market visibility and distinctiveness, and thus strong identifiability. In the market, consumers immediately associate the "Nikon" and "Nikang" marks with Nikon Corporation's relevant products. The defendant Zhejiang Nikang used the characters "Nikang" and "NICOM" on its website pages, store decoration designs, etc.; moreover, its product names were also named with "Nikang"; Zhejiang Nikang used the characters "Nikang" and "NICOM" on the bodies of the electric bicycles and electric tricycles it produced; Zhejiang Nikang used the words "Nikang Vehicle Industry", "Nikang Electric Bicycle", and "Nikang" at the entrance of its business office, outside the building, on the bodies of the company's vehicles, in advertising materials, and in the Nikang newspaper. These facts prove that the characters "Nikang" used by Zhejiang Nikang are identical to the registered trademark "Nikang" of Nikon Corporation, and the combination of English letters "NICOM" used, although not completely identical to the combination of English letters "Nikon" of Nikon Corporation's registered trademark, has similar pronunciation and letter combination structure. This use is sufficient to cause the relevant public to misidentify the source of the products. According to the provisions of Article 1(1)(2) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks, which states that "reproducing, imitating, or translating another person's registered well-known trademark or its main part for use as a trademark on dissimilar goods, misleading the public, and potentially harming the interests of the registrant of the well-known trademark constitutes an act of causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark as provided in Article 52(5) of the Trademark Law," it should be determined that Zhejiang Nikang's acts infringed the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks of Nikon Corporation. Zhejiang Nikang argued that the trademark it used was lawfully obtained and there was no possibility of misleading or confusing the public. Since Zhejiang Nikang's Trademark No. 1977805 "Nikang" has been revoked according to law, its claim lacks factual basis.

Furthermore, after obtaining the product brochure of the defendant Zhejiang Nikang from the Nikang electric vehicle sales counter in the defendant Taihua Market, Shanghai Huacheng Law Firm purchased two Nikang electric vehicles and obtained an "Electric Vehicle After-Sales Service Certificate" stamped with the seals of "Xi'an Xincheng District Jin Nikang Electric Bicycle Shop" and "Xi'an Taihua Electric Bicycle Wholesale Market Co., Ltd. Administrative Seal". The signboard at the entrance of Taihua Market read: "China Nikang Electric Vehicles Recruiting Dealers Nationwide", with "Nikang" and "NICOM" prominently highlighted. These facts prove that Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping jointly sold electric bicycles produced by Zhejiang Nikang. According to Article 52(1)(2) of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, selling goods that infringe the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is an act of infringement. The sales by Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping constituted infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation. Taihua Market argued that when Nikang electric vehicles entered the market operated by its company, relevant license certificates had been obtained, making them lawful goods. Since there is no direct causal relationship between obtaining relevant license certificates and goods being lawful, its defense cannot stand. As for Taihua Market's argument that the after-sales certificate provided by Nikon Corporation was an act of misleading Taihua Market, because Taihua Market did not provide evidence that Nikon Corporation had misled it, its claim is not accepted.

**III. Regarding whether the defendant Zhejiang Nikang's use of the characters "Nikang" in its enterprise name constituted unfair competition**

In this case, the plaintiff Nikon Corporation not only enjoys the right to the registered trademark "Nikang" but also the right to its enterprise name. The "Nikang" of Nikon Corporation, whether as a registered trademark or as a trade name, predates that of the defendant Zhejiang Nikang. Moreover, when Zhejiang Nikang changed its trade name to "Nikang" on June 27, 2006, Nikon Corporation already had certain market visibility and was known to the relevant public. Zhejiang Nikang's use of "Nikang" as a trade name had an obvious subjective intent to attach itself to the business reputation of Nikon Corporation. Its use of "Nikang" as a trade name in business operations is sufficient to mislead the relevant public into confusing, misidentifying, or associating Zhejiang Nikang and its products with Nikon Corporation. Therefore, Zhejiang Nikang constituted unfair competition against Nikon Corporation.

**IV. Regarding the assumption of civil liability in this case**

First, whether infringement should be stopped. The plaintiff Nikon Corporation requested that the defendants Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping stop selling electric vehicle products infringing its exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Nikang" and "Nikon", and that the defendant Zhejiang Nikang stop its acts infringing the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Nikang" and "Nikon". These requests have sufficient factual and legal basis and are supported according to law.

Second, whether the defendant Zhejiang Nikang should stop using the trade name "Nikang". After Zhejiang Nikang was registered and established on March 28, 2000 with "Wuxing" as its trade name, its products and the company received several awards, and the "Wuxing" trade name had a certain influence among consumers. Under these circumstances, on June 6, 2006, Zhejiang Nikang improperly registered the prior registered trademark and trade name "Nikang" of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation, which has high visibility, as the trade name in its own enterprise name. The act of registering and using "Nikang" was itself illegal. Based on the specific circumstances of this case, Zhejiang Nikang's use of "Nikang" as a trade name is sufficient to mislead the relevant public into confusing, misidentifying, or associating Zhejiang Nikang and its products with Nikon Corporation. Nikon Corporation's request that Zhejiang Nikang stop the unfair competition act of using the characters "Nikang" in its enterprise name should be supported.

Finally, the determination of the amount of damages in this case. The plaintiff Nikon Corporation requested that the defendant Zhejiang Nikang compensate it for losses of RMB 2,000,000, calculated based on Zhejiang Nikang's profits from 2005 to 2007. Since the amount of compensation for infringement should be calculated retroactively for two years from the date of filing of the lawsuit by Nikon Corporation, i.e., April 29, 2009, Nikon Corporation's request for damages from 2005 to 2007 is clearly inappropriate. Considering factors such as Zhejiang Nikang's degree of subjective fault, scale of operations, nature, scope, duration, and consequences of the infringement acts, and the reputation of the trademarks, the amount of compensation, including the reasonable expenses incurred by Nikon Corporation to stop the infringement, is determined to be RMB 200,000.

In summary, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 3, 52(1)(2), 52(5), and 56 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1(1)(2), 16, 17, 18, and 21 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks, Article 5(1)(3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Disputes over Conflicts Between Registered Trademarks, Enterprise Names, and Prior Rights, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 28, 2010:

1. The defendants Taihua Market and Zhu Guoping shall immediately cease selling electric vehicle products that infringe the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Nikang" and "Nikon" of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation upon the entry into force of this judgment;
2. The defendant Zhejiang Nikang shall immediately cease its acts of infringing the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Nikang" and "Nikon" of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation upon the entry into force of this judgment;
3. The defendant Zhejiang Nikang shall immediately cease using "Nikang" as the trade name in its enterprise name upon the entry into force of this judgment;
4. Within ten days after the entry into force of this judgment, the defendant Zhejiang Nikang shall compensate the plaintiff Nikon Corporation RMB 200,000 (including the reasonable expenses incurred by Nikon Corporation to stop the infringement);
5. The remaining claims of the plaintiff Nikon Corporation are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the parties did not appeal within the statutory period, and the first-instance judgment has taken legal effect.
